title: Opening a bank account
situation: You go to a bank in Korea to open your first account. You greet the teller, say what you need, and hand over your ID to fill out the form.
tip: At the counter, '계좌를 만들고 싶어요' or '계좌를 개설하려고 왔어요' both work. Foreigners usually need a 외국인등록증 (ARC) as 신분증.

turns.en: Welcome. How can I help you?

turns.prompt: Say you'd like to open a bank account.

choices.en: I'd like to open an account.
choices.feedback: -고 싶어요 states what service you want clearly and politely at the counter.

choices.en: Make me an account. (too casual/rude)
choices.feedback: The casual command 만들어 is rude to a bank employee.

choices.en: I need money. (wrong meaning)
choices.feedback: This says you need money; it does not ask to open an account.

turns.en: Sure, could you show me your ID, please?

turns.prompt: Hand over your ID and say 'here you are'. (You only have your foreigner ID card.)

choices.en: Here's my foreigner registration card.
choices.feedback: 여기 N이요 is a concise, polite way to hand over the requested document.

choices.en: I don't have an ID. (then you can't open one)
choices.feedback: This contradicts the situation because you do have your foreigner registration card.

choices.en: My passport is at home. (unhelpful)
choices.feedback: This does not hand over the ID you have with you, so the transaction cannot continue.

turns.en: Thank you. Please fill out this application form.

turns.prompt: Ask where you should write your phone number on the form.

choices.en: Where should I write my phone number?
choices.feedback: 어디에 적으면 돼요? asks for the exact place on the form naturally and politely.

choices.en: I don't know the phone number. (odd)
choices.feedback: This says you do not know the number instead of asking where to write it.

choices.en: Do I write all of this? (vague)
choices.feedback: 이거 and 다 are too vague; the question must identify the phone-number field.

turns.ko: 여기 이름 옆에 적어 주시면 돼요. 체크카드도 함께 만들어 드릴까요?
turns.en: Just write it next to your name. Shall I make you a debit card too?

turns.prompt: Say yes, and ask if there's a fee.

choices.en: Yes, please make one. Is there a fee?
choices.feedback: This accepts the card offer and follows with the practical fee question in polite speech.

choices.en: No, just the bankbook. I hate cards. (blunt)
choices.feedback: This rejects the card and does not ask about the fee; 카드 싫어요 also sounds unnecessarily blunt.

choices.en: What's a card? (unnatural here)
choices.feedback: The employee already offered a specific debit card, so this broad question is unnatural and misses the fee prompt.

turns.ko: 카드 발급 수수료는 없어요. 통장과 카드는 잠시 후에 나옵니다.
turns.en: There is no card issuance fee. Your bankbook and card will be ready in a moment.

title: Getting a document at the district office
situation: You visit the 구청 (district office) to apply for and pick up an official document. You take a number, submit your papers, and ask when it will be ready.
tip: At a 구청 or immigration office, take a 번호표 first and wait for your number. Use '신청하다' to apply, '발급받다' to get a document issued, and '접수하다' for them processing/receiving it.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요. 번호표 뽑고 잠시 기다려 주세요.
turns.en: Hello. Please take a number and wait a moment.

turns.prompt: Ask where the number-ticket machine is.

choices.en: Where do I take a number ticket?
choices.feedback: 어디에서 뽑아요? asks for the ticket machine's location clearly and politely.

choices.en: Give me a number. (too casual/rude)
choices.feedback: 줘 is a casual command to the staff member and does not ask where the machine is.

choices.en: What's the number? (confusing)
choices.feedback: This asks what a number is, not where to take a number ticket.

turns.ko: 입구 오른쪽에 있어요. 다음 손님, 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
turns.en: It's on the right at the entrance. Next customer, how can I help you?

turns.prompt: Say you came to apply for a certificate of residence (a document).

choices.en: I came to get a copy of my resident registration issued.
choices.feedback: Naming the document and using -으러 왔어요 tells the clerk exactly why you came.

choices.en: Give me the document, quickly. (impolite)
choices.feedback: The document is not identified, and 빨리요 makes the request sound impatient.

choices.en: Do you have documents here? (vague)
choices.feedback: 서류 is too vague, and this does not explain that you came to have one issued.

turns.en: Sure, could you give me your ID and the application form?

turns.prompt: Hand them over and say you've already filled out the form.

choices.en: Here you are. I filled out the form in advance.
choices.feedback: 여기 있어요 hands over both items, and 미리 작성했어요 gives the requested status clearly.

choices.en: I didn't fill it out, just give it to me. (won't work)
choices.feedback: This refuses the required form and demands the document without completing the process.

choices.en: Is this right? (too vague)
choices.feedback: 이거 does not identify the ID or form, and the sentence never says the form is complete.

turns.en: I've processed your application. The fee is 1,000 won.

turns.prompt: Pay, and ask when the document will be ready.

choices.ko: 여기요. 서류는 언제 받을 수 있을까요?
choices.en: Here you go. When will I be able to receive the document?
choices.feedback: 여기요 accompanies the payment, and -을 수 있을까요? asks the ready time politely.

choices.en: Why is it so expensive? (rude over 1,000 won)
choices.feedback: This complains about the stated fee and never asks when the document will be ready.

choices.en: Give it to me right now. (demanding)
choices.feedback: 지금 당장 주세요 is a demand and ignores the processing time.

turns.ko: 십 분 정도 걸려요. 성함을 부르면 이쪽으로 와 주세요.
turns.en: It takes about ten minutes. When I call your name, please come over here.
